newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW - NOKIA CEO UPBEAT ON H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - NOKIA CEO UPBEAT ON H2.

text.p: Europe's leading mobile phone maker Nokia said on Monday it increased its market share during the second quarter and beat its target handset profit margins of over 10 percent.

"We have strengthened our market position, we have increased our market share, we are happy with the growth we have encountered and we have strengthened our number one position," CEO Jorma Ollila told Reuters after the company's Q2 report.
"We are pleased with the second quarter and that gives us an extremely good platform for the second half of the year," Ollila said in an interview.
"We maintain a strongly positive outlook. We look forward in a very positive mode for next six month period," he said.

"We did better than our target of 10 percent in mobile phones, we improved our profits in infrastructure as well as in the other business, so it was an overall very strong performance throughout the company," he said.

Asked about the outlook for handset margins in H2, Ollila said: "It's difficult to forecast. I think the market is continuing to be very competitive (but) I think we have a very strong product offering for all the regions. We are very confident about how our market position will be also in the second half."
Ollila highlighted Nokia's above-market growth in its telecommunications infrastructure business as a feature of the first-half profit, which at 3.33 billion markka just beat market forecasts.

"We feel very good about our market position in the infrastructure business because we are gaining good orders both on the new operators as well as on the existing customers," he said. "So that ... is the other significant feature."
Asked what role foreign exchange gains had played in Nokia's Q2 profit surge, he said: "It's not dramatic. But we have gained somewhat and benefitted from the strength of the dollar."

He declined any comment on future product launches Nokia may plan to rival handset newcomers, but said: "In every respect we are confident that our product range will be a very strong one, as it was in the first six months."
Asked for the growth outlook further ahead in Nokia's two main businesses -- mobile phones and telecoms infrastructure -- he said Nokia's forecasts of 25-35 percent were conservative.

"I think -- what we have said in the past is that this year and next year we expect our major businesses to grow between 25 and 35 percent ... and that's obviously the target we seem to be meeting and it's a slightly conservative one, so we will look at it with optimism in the future."
He added that sales of Nokia's Communicator 9000, which combines data, fax, internet and e-mail communications with wireless voice, were meeting targets.
And Nokia's new Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) digital mobile phone, currently being shipped to United States markets, will be in the shops in "a matter of a week or two", he added.
